messages:
anika: FYI support -> large p95/p99 spike reported for hosted text-generation API starting ~22:10 UTC after the maintenance window. Customers hitting timeouts. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/hosted/p95-p99 (prod/us-west1). p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms, p99 from ~320ms to ~2.4s. Can SRE / infra triage?

alex: I'm on it. Any obvious correlation with deploys or infra changes?

sre-bot: deploys: no model or API code deploys at 22:00-22:15. Kernel update job finished at 21:58 on a subset of hosts (linux-5.15 -> 6.6.x). GPU firmware rollout started 20:50 but only ~10% completed.

maria: Confirming: no application changes. Support says errors are latency-related (timeouts) not 5xx product errors. Customers report prolonged stalls while tokens are being generated.

jonah: grabbing traces from runtime. Can you drop a sample request id?

anika: sample request ids: req_4b9a, req_4b9b (from customer X). Happened on host node gpu-prod-uw-17.

alex: ssh'ing into gpu-prod-uw-17 now. Running iostat and nvme checks.

alex: (output) `sudo iostat -x 1 5`
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         45.00  12.00  1800.00  240.00   40.00    8.63   18.12  12.40  45.20  0.50  4.50
nvme1n1         12.00   2.00   480.00   16.00   36.00    0.02    1.70   0.90   2.50  0.11  0.20

alex: avgqu-sz for nvme0n1 is high on that host. Also seeing `blk_mq` messages in dmesg: `[  1234.567890] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678`.

maria: interesting — those errors line up with kernel update window. Could be a driver/kernel/firmware compatibility issue. Any CUDA driver updates?

anika: We rolled out CUDA 12.1 -> 12.3 on a different schedule earlier this week but not in that window. Only kernel + some vendor firmware.

jonah: checking runtime logs for token service on that host. Seeing repeated stalls when KV cache fetching from local disk layer is slow. Token generation CPU/GPU doesn't block, but feeder thread waits on I/O.

paul: can we confirm whether models use on-disk mmap for shards or if we have prefetch enabled? If mmap'd and the kernel changed pagecache behavior it could magnify tail latency.

alex: runtime config: model_shard_load = mmap; prefetch_enabled = true for big models.

maria: two-prong approach: 1) Immediate mitigation: disable prefetch on hosts with kernel 6.6.x and bump I/O queue depth for nvme0; 2) Long term: rollback kernel on affected pool and coordinate with vendor for nvme firmware compatibility.

anika: Is disabling prefetch safe in prod? Will increase memory pressure and cold-start latencies but reduces tail stalls.

jonah: I can push a host-level hotfix: `/opt/runtime/bin/runtimectl set-config --prefetch=false` on targeted hosts and restart feeder service only (no model reload). That should be non-disruptive for existing cached models.

alex: performing kernel rollback on one canary host now (gpu-prod-uw-19). Rolling to previous kernel 5.15. Rebooting.

sre-bot: Canaries: rolling rollback initiated on gpu-prod-uw-19 (21:45 UTC).

alex: rollback complete, host back. iostat on gpu-prod-uw-19 shows nvme0n1 avgqu-sz ~0.05, await ~1.9ms. Grafana shows p99 on that host dropped back to ~300ms for a short window.

maria: good signal. Proceed to rollback other affected hosts in the pool. Meanwhile jonah, push the prefetch=false hotfix to hosts that can't be rebooted immediately.

jonah: pushed prefetch=false to 6 hosts in pool and restarted feeder threads. Initial metrics: p95 down to ~180ms, p99 ~420ms. Still higher than baseline but customers are recoverable.

anika: support to customers: "We identified an infra-level kernel/firmware interaction that caused storage I/O tail latency. We've applied mitigations (targeted kernel rollback and runtime prefetch disable) and are monitoring. We're prioritizing a permanent fix with infra vendor."

paul: action items: (1) coordinate with vendor for NVMe firmware + kernel repro (owner: infra/alex), (2) test full fleet rollback vs vendor patch (owner: eng-infra), (3) update runtime to avoid blocking on pagecache sync path (owner: eng-runtime/jonah), (4) add alerting rule for avgqu-sz nvme > 2 and correlation with host kernel version (owner: eng-sre/maria).

maria: filing incident ticket I-2026-772 with timeline and initial root cause hypothesis: kernel 6.6+ changed NVMe/blk_mq behavior interacting poorly with our mmap+prefetch pattern, causing queue-depth blowups and p99 token-generation latency spikes.

anika: posting to customers channel and escalating to enterprise accounts impacted. Will follow up with postmortem once vendor confirms root cause. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

paul: one more note — we'll also add a short-term routing policy to prefer Dedicated pools for customers with strict latency SLAs during infra rollouts. Low friction and provides SLA protection until fix is validated.

sre-bot: incident updated: status -> mitigated; monitoring -> watch.

anika: I'll keep this thread open for updates. If you hit any regressions after rollback/fix, paste logs here.

jonah: quick snippet of the runtime patch I'm proposing to avoid stalls (preliminary):
```
- /* blocking read from disk */
- read_shard_sync();
+ /* async fallback: try pagecache, then schedule background fetch */
+ if (!pagecache_has(shard)) schedule_background_fetch(shard);
```
will submit PR after initial tests.

maria: thanks. closing timeline note: first alert 22:12 UTC, mitigations applied 22:58 UTC (prefetch toggle), canary rollback 23:03 UTC, broad rollback ongoing.

anika: closing for now, will reopen if any p99 spikes reappear.
